prompts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one hand-drawn expression key cel for an owl game's idle animation. IMAGE 1 is the locked game character and body pose to edit. IMAGE 2 is the user's crucial EXPRESSION AND FEATHER-POSE reference, not a style reference. Make image 1 suddenly wear image 2's very funny long-eared, vacant, awkwardly alert owl expression. The two existing big feather brows/ear tufts must perk almost STRAIGHT VERTICALLY UP like the two tall upright rabbit-ear tufts in the photograph; do not retain their wide swept sideways V configuration. Keep them as feather tufts of the same owl, NOT literal mammal ears. Flatten the puffiness of the upper face feathers inward just enough to create the photograph's comical narrow, tall, serious face. Expose round amber eyes with the SAME iris/pupil scale and simple highlights as the original game owl, giving a blank deadpan stare; do NOT make enlarged sparkling baby eyes or a cute plush expression. The combination is ears sticking straight up, a solemn skinny-looking face and ridiculous surprised alertness, inspired closely by the photograph. Keep the head anchored and the beak closed at the original location. Redraw forehead, feather roots and revealed eye sockets coherently, no cutout transforms. Preserve game sprite style: warm taupe/brown patterned feathers, cream facial markings, dark teal contours and original shading. Preserve image 1's entire chest, folded wing, feet, talons, tail, perched stance, body size, canvas registration and camera angle exactly. No skinny-body transformation, no movement below the neck. No smile, human eyebrows, teeth, blush, icons, text or props; no photographic rendering or background from image 2. Full-body single sprite on the original 1254-square transparent canvas. Keep both vertical tufts complete with transparent margin above. Produce the funny extreme key pose, one cel only.

Use case: precise-object-edit. ONE exact registered 2D owl animation key cel. EDIT IMAGE 1, not image 2. Image 1 is the original locked game sprite; image 2 supplies ONLY the comical vertically erect feather-tuft gesture. The previous expression concept incorrectly turned the face toward the camera. CORRECT that: retain image 1's original THREE-QUARTER FACE ANGLE looking toward the VIEWER'S LEFT, its beak on the LEFT SIDE of the face rather than centered, and the farther left eye smaller/narrower than the nearer right eye. Keep original cheek contours, original head dimensions, original beak silhouette, original beak location, original iris size and original gaze direction. The beak must stay near horizontal pixel 400, never move to the center x520. Only change the original downward slanted long feather brows into two nearly VERTICAL, perked, tall tufts with coherent roots that expose rounded, deadpan amber eyes, evoking an absurdly alert long-eared owl. Preserve original tuft lengths and feather colors; the brow tips point UP, not sideways. The funny effect comes from the upright tufts and vacant alert eyes. Do not use baby proportions, large sparkly eyes or a smile. All stationary body artwork, head outline below the brow roots, cheek feather shapes, beak, chest, wings, tail, feet and talons MUST be identical to image 1 in position, anatomy, palette, feather pattern and rendering. No transformation of body proportions or pose, no face rotation, no new props or background, no text. Full-body sprite, original 1254 by 1254 transparent canvas. Actual drawn new feather-brow pose and upper-eye exposure, not transformed cutouts.

Use case: precise-object-edit. EDIT IMAGE 1 with a small but crucial facial-expression correction. Keep its two vertical upright feather tufts, entire head angle, cheeks, beak, body, wing, tail, feet, palette and transparent canvas exactly as drawn. Image 2 is the user's expression reference. Image 1 still has an ANGRY V-shaped brow pressing down on its eyes, which is WRONG. Remove that stern squint: LIFT THE INNER BROW ROOTS from the bridge of the beak upward toward the forehead, revealing both entire round amber eyes. Show a visibly surprised, vacant, absurdly serious 'Huh?' stare like image 2. The top arc of each iris should be visible. Keep the irises and pupils the same size and place; they become rounder by removing the brow occlusion, not by enlarging or translating the eyes. Fill the newly exposed forehead, eyelid and eye-socket artwork smoothly. The central feather wedge must retract upward, so it no longer slopes down onto the top halves of the eyes. Preserve a subtle three-quarter view, with the far eye narrower. No remaining scowling V-shaped eyebrow. Do not change the beak at all. Do not turn the head. No cute baby eyes, giant highlights, mouth, smile, text, new eyebrows or props. A single drawn 1254 by 1254 full-body transparent sprite with only the brow roots and eye opening changed.
